fatal_errors: The proposed dealloying route does not reconstruct the reported spray-drying/thermal decomposition-reduction method.
The initial material, acidic or alkaline dissolution conditions, and selective-dissolution mechanism conflict with the aqueous salt precursors and hydrogen reduction at 300°C used in the target work.
Selective removal of less-noble constituents could destroy the intended high-entropy composition rather than form a compositionally homogeneous single-phase HEA.
No evidence is cited to establish that dealloying produces the specified noble-metal HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad goal of making a porous three-dimensional catalytic framework and proposes a generally testable dealloying experiment. However, it misses the central synthesis and rationale of the target: homogeneous precursor salts are spray-dried and reduced in H2, with early reduction of Pt, Ir, or Ru creating a lattice and dissociated hydrogen assisting incorporation of Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe into a single-phase solid solution. It also omits the relevant temperature regime, noble-metal-dependent boundaries, Pt–Ru fcc/hcp phase tuning, and Pt-black catalytic comparison. The predicted high surface area and enhanced activity overlap only at a generic outcome level. Because the alternative is uncited and may remove enough elements to compromise HEA identity, it is not sufficiently supported as a valid alternative answer.
